title: Learning Hamiltonian Flow Maps: Mean Flow Consistency for Large-Timestep Molecular Dynamics
claim: Prior methods need costly simulated trajectories and yield fixed jumps; ours trains directly on independent samples and supports arbitrary jumps.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, gray standard versus blue ours, shared input box
description: A wide figure with two horizontal bands sharing a rounded input box on the left, labeled Ab-initio Data (decorrelated), with molecule renderings annotated by force and position arrows. The top gray band, 'Standard Approach / Trajectory-Based', flows right through Train Teacher (MLFF), a red-outlined 'Long Trajectories' box with a warning sign and snail icon marking slow simulation, then Training Pairs, and finally a Large-Timestep Model labeled Discrete with a fixed jump. The bottom blue band, 'Our Approach / Tailored Loss Formulation', uses a rocket icon and a straight blue arrow for direct training with only instantaneous labels. It passes through a dashed box showing purple and cyan phase-space curves for x and p, and ends at a Continuous model with a slider labeled Arbitrary Jump. Loss formulas appear in each band. The eye goes first to the bold titles and the contrast between the gray and blue bands.
caption: Hamiltonian Flow Maps (HFMs) for large timesteps in phase space. Top row: Existing approaches rely on trajectory data, typically generated using a teacher MLFF through sequential simulation with small timesteps. While this enables training large-timestep models via direct regression, the resulting models are limited to a fixed set of predefined timesteps that cannot be adjusted after training. Bottom row: Our approach learns continuous-time, large-timestep dynamics directly from decorrelated ab-initio samples, without requiring trajectories. The model supports arbitrary timesteps at inference. Our tailored loss combines force matching with a consistency constraint that enforces agreement of the predicted flow across different time horizons (see Section 4.2).
abstract: Simulating the long-time evolution of Hamiltonian systems is limited by the small timesteps required for stable numerical integration. To overcome this constraint, we introduce a framework to learn Hamiltonian Flow Maps by predicting the mean phase-space evolution over a chosen time span, enabling stable large-timestep updates far beyond the stability limits of classical integrators. To this end, we impose a Mean Flow consistency condition for time-averaged Hamiltonian dynamics. Unlike prior approaches, this allows training on independent phase-space samples without access to future states, avoiding expensive trajectory generation. Validated across diverse Hamiltonian systems, our method in particular improves upon molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learned force fields (MLFF). Our models maintain comparable training and inference cost, but support significantly larger integration timesteps while trained directly on widely-available trajectory-free MLFF datasets.
